headline: OpenAI pitches AI campuses as power plant protectors
summary: The AI giant is rebranding its data centers and promising to supply up to 1,000 megawatts of power during emergencies, aiming to quell public opposition.
details: OpenAI is piloting its "Grid Protectors Program" to address growing public backlash against data centers. The initiative aims to reframe these facilities not as polluters, but as community assets by promising to provide up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies.

This move comes as opposition to data centers mounts across the US, fueled by concerns over their massive energy consumption and environmental impact. Residents have protested projects, citing worries about electricity demand and heat generation. Several states have also enacted laws to prevent AI companies from passing on energy costs to consumers.

OpenAI is rebranding its data centers as "compute campuses" to distance them from their negative public perception. The company argues that their consistent year-round power demand can help stabilize the grid and spread fixed costs for utilities.

The "Grid Protectors Program" seeks to create mutually beneficial arrangements with utility services. OpenAI plans to reduce demand when the grid is strained, potentially lowering costs for customers and improving grid reliability during peak usage times.
The company is also partnering with Oracle and SoftBank to build "Stargate" data centers across the US, including locations in Georgia, Texas, and New Mexico, as part of its expansion plans.

headline_marked: [[Putin demands]] 10% of Russian data center capacity for state use
headline: Putin demands 10% of Russian data center capacity for state use
summary: Private data centers in Russia must reserve 10% of their capacity for state IT infrastructure with 24 hours' notice, following a directive from President Putin.
details: President Vladimir Putin has ordered non-state data centers in Russia to reserve 10% of their capacity for the government. This move aims to quickly provide additional compute power to state IT infrastructure if needed.
The directive comes amid increased Ukrainian drone attacks targeting Russian data centers, which have caused significant damage and disrupted services, including those of Yandex.

Following recent attacks on major facilities and the Russian finance ministry's data center, Putin has tasked the Digital Development Ministry with inventorying all available private data center capacity.

A new government commission will have the authority to order the release of this reserved capacity, with third-party owners given 24 hours to comply. The use of data centers outside Russia is also being considered, pending security service approval.
This development occurs as Russia's Federal State Statistics Service reported a cyberattack that resulted in the theft of 23TB of data, including sensitive wartime loss information.
